- The depended-on hub does not mention the refund or that anything waits on it.

- `groom_cancellation_no_show`: superseded clause "A late cancellation carries late_cancel_fee_usd, or ... forfeits one visit instead of the fee" → `cancellation_and_no_show_terms` Section 3 "(former wording, no longer in force) ... superseded by the current basis for late cancellations on prepaid passes and on Groom Club Monthly" — retired, still borne. Unnamed clauses carried in force: Sections 1, 2 (free notice, full elapsed hours, exactly-notice free), 4 (remedy recorded on the cancellation), 5 (no-show forfeits, no fee on top), 6 (salon cancellations), 7 (once per booking). Per-tier figures in `cancellation_attendance_terms` match the variants (24/24/24/24/48/24 h; 15/15/20/20/25/0; forfeits-visit only on the club; grace 15).
- `groom_pass_cancel_refund`: superseded full-refund clause → `pass_cancellation_terms` Clause 4 (retired); superseded partial-refund clause (single-visit price basis) → Clause 5 (retired); club clause (superseded by the sibling extended policy) → Clause 6 (retired). In force: Clause 1 (only the customer), Clause 2 (status active or suspended, table), Clause 3 (original payment).
- Remaining base charter (all borne, figures checked cell by cell against `variants[].parameters`): multi-holding → `one_live_pass_per_pet`; household discounts → `household_pass_discounts`; pricing → `pass_pricing_at_purchase` + `pass_lineup_prices`; booking → `appointment_booking_requirements` + `booking_terms`; visit charges → `visit_checkout_charges` + `checkout_surcharges` + `addon_price_list`; redo → `satisfaction_redo`; club billing → `club_monthly_billing` + `club_membership_terms`; expiry (offset 0) → `pass_expiry_and_extension` + `pass_refund_transfer_expiry_terms`; transfers → `pass_transfer_between_pets`; rewards → `rewards_points_on_grooming`. ## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the 11 task-relevant documents (2 hubs, 2 baselines, 11 factor docs counting shared facets) traces to the rule, compute, params or tool contract above. Notable derived statements checked: "Only the pass in question is counted" (COUNT scoped to the pass); "The weekday of the day the cancellation was recorded plays no part" (appointment date per source); "including any extension already granted" (`expires_on` on the record); "Every free redo entry ... counts once, whichever visit it redid" (COUNT groom_redo); Autoship "across all of them" (household XCOUNT) — all entailed, none adds a condition.
- Additions / rewrites / omissions: none at entailment level.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. The blocked hub names only its own tool; the depended-on hub names only its own tool.
- A task's opening world state written in as policy fact: none (no reference to a specific pass, appointment, Saturday 3 October, 15 hours, deshedding booking, etc.; all examples are labelled hypothetical and use other values).
- Observations (not defects):
  - O1: the source sentence listing the fee's inputs ("worked out from that cancellation ..., the booking it names, the pass history and the customer's other Tailwise programs") has no prose home. Its content is entailed by the six factor documents; rendering it on the hub would itself signal that variations exist. No semantic loss.
  - O2: retired Clause 4 describes the former clause including "that window counted in calendar days from the purchase date as day 0 and a request on the last day in time". The base sentence on window counting was not itself named in the overwrite, but the same counting is re-enacted by the extended policy's replaced_by and stands in force in refund schedule A ("that date being day 0 ... A request on the last day of the window is in time"). Net in-force semantics unchanged; recorded for transparency, not as KB legislation.
